notes.4: For this exercise, candidates were required to read a more extended text about Arnaud who decided to change his job. The text used largely familiar vocabulary. Overall, candidates performed well on this exercise. The text was written in the first person, and the questions used the third person. Most questions could be answered by lifting a small number of words from the text, but some answers also required a minor manipulation. If candidates choose to lift more than is required to answer questions, they must make any manipulation needed in the extra material, for example replacing je with il and changing the verb if necessary. Candidates are therefore advised to answer with the minimum number of words. Overall, candidates answered this question well. For 4(a) , some candidates miscopied mois , which created another word in French ( moi , moins ), and could not gain the mark. For 4(b) , some candidates did not understand où in the question and answered with Il travaillait comme programmeur , which did not answer the question. For 4(e) , some candidates offered long and largely irrelevant answers, showing a misunderstanding of the question.
notes.5: In this question, candidates had to match a series of descriptions with statements from people looking for a film festival. Candidates had five people and eight descriptions to choose from. Candidates had to process a Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French November 2023 variety of information and match several requirements whilst eliminating responses that did not fit. The question is aimed at the higher grades, and candidates with a wide range of vocabulary and knowledge of synonyms performed well on this section. Each person’s statement gave quite specific requirements for what they were looking for, such as price, time of day and type of film. It is important for candidates to note that these details excluded all answers except the correct one. Candidates need to ensure they consider all the information given as this is not a gist comprehension question and a global understanding of the texts will not be sufficient. Description 5 was a frequent incorrect answer for 5(a) : the opening time did not match Hélène’s requirements.
notes.6: This final exercise about Christelle’s experience of voluntary work with older people was intended to be the most challenging part of the paper. About half the questions could be answered with a careful lift from the text, the others needed a small manipulation of the text. Very few candidates achieved full marks, and the questions seem to have discriminated appropriately. Only a few candidates left some of their answers blank. Although verbs do not necessarily have to be correct to score a mark, the tense usually must be appropriate to the question. Candidates are reminded that the questions follow the order of the text, therefore early questions are unlikely to be answered by words from the final paragraph, and vice versa. Overall, candidates answered this question well. For 6(d) , 6(e) and 6(f) , some candidates lifted the wrong part of the text and others did not manipulate the text. For 6(h) , some candidates omitted proche and invalidated their otherwise correct answer. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French November 2023
